title: Children's and neonatal maintenance fluids (Holliday-Segar, mL/kg/day)
blurb: Calculate a child's 24-hour maintenance fluid with the Holliday-Segar bands, a newborn's mL/kg/day volume, and the hourly pump rate.
question: A child weighing 14 kg needs maintenance intravenous fluids. Using the Holliday-Segar rule, what volume is needed over 24 hours?

teach.body: Formal rule (NICE NG29): routine maintenance fluid is 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg. Plain English: split the weight into bands, work out each band, then add. Divide the daily total by 24 for the pump rate. The rule is always printed in a Part A stem; you supply the arithmetic.

head: Weight band
mL/kg/day
Band maximum
teach.caption: NG29: over 24 hours, males rarely need more than 2,500 mL and females more than 2,000 mL.

teach.h: Worked example: Noah on a children's ward
teach.body: Noah Bennett, 6, weighs 26 kg and needs maintenance IV fluids. First 10 kg: 10 × 100 = 1000 mL. Next 10 kg: 10 × 50 = 500 mL. Remaining 6 kg: 6 × 20 = 120 mL. Total = 1620 mL a day. Rate = 1620 ÷ 24 = 67.5, which rounds to 68 mL per hour. Sense-check: under the 2,000 to 2,500 mL ceiling.

teach.caption: Only the kilograms above 20 go into the 20 mL/kg band.

teach.text: Applying one rate to the whole weight. A 26 kg child is not 26 × 100 or 26 × 20: the bands stack. And only the kilograms over 20 get 20 mL/kg; using the full 26 kg in the last band adds 400 mL too much.

teach.h: Term newborns: mL/kg/day by day of life (NG29)
head: Day of life
mL/kg/day
teach.caption: The stem gives the exact mL/kg/day to use. Convert grams to kg first.

teach.body: A fluid bolus for resuscitation is a single volume, not a daily rate: NG29 gives 10 mL/kg of glucose-free crystalloid over less than 10 minutes. A 21 kg child's bolus is 21 × 10 = 210 mL. Do not divide a bolus by 24.

items.label: daily volume to mL per hour

items: Add the bands for the daily total, then ÷ 24 for mL per hour.
Newborns: weight (kg) × the mL/kg/day in the stem.
Apply a stated cap (for example 2000 mL a day) before dividing.
A bolus (10 mL/kg) is a single volume, not a daily rate.

summary: You can now calculate children's maintenance fluids with the Holliday-Segar bands, newborn volumes from mL/kg/day, and the hourly pump rate. You can also apply a stated daily cap and tell a maintenance rate from a bolus.

A.q: A child weighing 9 kg needs maintenance intravenous fluids. Use the Holliday-Segar rule: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg. What volume is needed over 24 hours? Please use the correct unit.
A.why: 9 kg is all in the first band: 9 × 100 = 900 mL over 24 hours.

whyNot.0: This uses the second band rate (50 mL/kg) for the first 10 kg.
whyNot.2: This adds a zero, a tenfold error.
whyNot.3: This uses the third band rate (20 mL/kg).

A.q: A child weighing 14 kg needs maintenance intravenous fluids. Use the Holliday-Segar rule: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg. What volume is needed over 24 hours? Please use the correct unit.
A.why: First 10 kg: 1000 mL. Next 4 kg: 4 × 50 = 200 mL. Total = 1200 mL.

whyNot.0: This uses 100 mL/kg for the whole weight.
whyNot.1: This uses 50 mL/kg for the whole weight.
whyNot.2: This uses 20 mL/kg for the kilograms between 10 and 20.

A.q: A child weighing 26 kg needs maintenance intravenous fluids over 24 hours. Use the Holliday-Segar rule: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
A.why: 1000 + 500 + (6 × 20) = 1620 mL a day. 1620 ÷ 24 = 67.5, which rounds up to 68 mL per hour.

whyNot.1: This rounds 67.5 down; a 5 rounds up.
whyNot.2: This uses 100 mL/kg for the whole weight.
whyNot.3: This is the daily volume, not the hourly rate.

B.q: A term baby on day 3 of life weighs 3.2 kg and is prescribed intravenous fluids at 90 mL/kg/day. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour?
B.why: 3.2 × 90 = 288 mL a day. 288 ÷ 24 = 12 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This is the daily volume, not the hourly rate.
whyNot.3: This leaves out the baby's weight.

B.q: A child weighing 21 kg is prescribed an intravenous fluid bolus of 0.9% sodium chloride 10 mL/kg. What volume should be given? Please use the correct unit.
B.why: 21 × 10 = 210 mL, given once as a bolus.

whyNot.1: This uses 100 mL/kg, the maintenance band rate, not the bolus.
whyNot.2: This divides a single bolus by 24 as if it were a daily volume.

B.q: A child weighing 34 kg needs maintenance intravenous fluids. Use the Holliday-Segar rule: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg. What volume is needed over 24 hours? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This puts the whole 34 kg into the third band instead of the 14 kg over 20.
whyNot.2: This uses 20 mL/kg for the whole weight.
whyNot.3: This uses 100 mL/kg for the whole weight.

C.q: A girl weighing 48 kg needs maintenance intravenous fluids. Use the Holliday-Segar rule: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg. The prescriber caps her total at 2000 mL in 24 hours. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
C.why: Holliday-Segar gives 1000 + 500 + (28 × 20) = 2060 mL, above the 2000 mL cap, so use 2000 mL. 2000 ÷ 24 = 83.33, so 83 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This uses 2060 mL and misses the 2000 mL cap.
whyNot.1: This uses 100 mL/kg for the whole weight.
whyNot.2: This rounds 83.33 up; it rounds down to 83.

C.q: A term baby on day 2 of life weighs 2750 g and is prescribed intravenous fluids at 75 mL/kg/day. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

whyNot.0: This cuts off 8.59 instead of rounding up.
whyNot.2: This uses the weight in grams as if it were kg.
whyNot.3: This is the daily volume, not the hourly rate.

C.q: A child weighing 22 kg needs maintenance intravenous fluids over 24 hours. Use the Holliday-Segar rule: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

whyNot.0: This uses 100 mL/kg for the whole weight.
whyNot.1: This uses 50 mL/kg for all 12 kg over 10, missing the third band.
whyNot.3: This rounds 64.17 up; it rounds down to 64.

reteach.title: Stack the bands
reteach.question: A child weighs 17 kg. How do you split the weight for Holliday-Segar?

blocks.body: 17 kg = first 10 kg + 7 kg. 10 × 100 = 1000 mL; 7 × 50 = 350 mL. Total 1350 mL a day.

blocks.h: 17 kg child: mL per day by band

blocks.text: 17 × 100 = 1700 mL treats every kilogram as if it were in the first band.

test.q: A child weighing 7 kg needs maintenance intravenous fluids. Use the Holliday-Segar rule: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg. What volume is needed over 24 hours? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This uses the second band rate.
whyNot.1: This uses the third band rate.
whyNot.3: This uses 10 mL/kg, the bolus volume.

test.q: A child weighs 17 kg. Use the Holliday-Segar rule: 100 mL/kg/day for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg/day for each kg over 20 kg. What volume does the second band (the kilograms between 10 and 20) contribute over 24 hours? Please use the correct unit.
test.why: 17 − 10 = 7 kg in the second band. 7 × 50 = 350 mL.

whyNot.1: This uses the whole weight instead of the 7 kg in the band.
whyNot.2: This uses the first band rate.
whyNot.3: This is the full daily total, not the second band alone.
